issues.description: The method Milkable.messageOnMilk() has conflicting return types between the problem statement and the code. The UML and task text in problem_statement.md declare messageOnMilk() as returning boolean and state "The method messageOnMilk() should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise" (problem_statement.md lines 51-53 and 92-94). In the provided solution code, the Milkable interface declares messageOnMilk() returning a String (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5), and the concrete classes (Seal, Goat) implement it to return printable messages (String). The template/solution Main also calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk()), which expects a printable value (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 30-32). This contradiction will either cause compilation errors or confuse students about which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type for Milkable.messageOnMilk() consistent across the specification and code. Recommended (preserves existing code and examples): update the problem statement and UML to declare messageOnMilk(): String and change the textual description to explain it returns a milking message (for example: "returns a printable message such as 'Goat <name> is milked'"). Update the task text where it currently says to return true/false. Alternatively (less recommended): change the solution and template code to use a boolean return type and adjust calls (e.g., do not print the boolean directly) and update examples/tests accordingly. Ensure the UML, textual description, interface declaration, and example call sites all use the same signature.
